name: b Aquilae
description: A naked-eye star 15.2 parsecs away, 1.4 times the Sun's width: its disc was measured with the CHARA Array.

radius.source: Boyajian et al. (2012), ApJ 746, 101, HD 182572: radius in solar radii, from the limb-darkened angular diameter 0.845 +/- 0.025 mas (CHARA) and the Hipparcos parallax, 1.379 +/- 0.042

mass.source: Boyajian et al. (2012), ApJ 746, 101, HD 182572: mass in solar masses, from Yonsei-Yale isochrones at the measured radius and temperature (a model value), 1.186 +/- 0.015

temperature.source: Boyajian et al. (2012), ApJ 746, 101, HD 182572: effective temperature in K, from the angular diameter and the bolometric flux, 5787 +/- 92

distance.source: Boyajian et al. (2012), ApJ 746, 101, HD 182572: the Hipparcos parallax the radius was computed with (van Leeuwen 2007), 65.89 +/- 0.26 mas, inverted

text.card: A naked-eye star 15 parsecs away whose disc the CHARA Array measured: 1.4 times the Sun's width.
text.introduction: Its disc spans 0.845 milliarcseconds, which gives 1.379 solar radii and 5,787 K at its surface.
text.locator: Tables 5 and 10, HD 182572: limb-darkened diameter, R, Teff
